summary.headline: Aeroflex Q2 FY27 revenue crossed INR200 crores for the first time, with total income of INR207.68 crores, up 87% YoY, and PAT of INR36.56 crores.
summary.overview: Management reported record Q2 FY27 total income of INR207.68 crores (up 87% YoY), EBITDA of INR50.34 crores (up 94%, margin 24.27%) and PAT of INR36.56 crores (up 157%, margin 17.6%). H1 FY27 total income was INR353.66 crores (up 81%), with H1 EBITDA of INR83.83 crores and PAT of INR55.35 crores, already close to full-year FY26 performance. The company changed depreciation from WDV to SLM from 1 April 2026, reducing depreciation by INR8.41 crores in both Q2 and H1. It also announced a total capex of INR202 crores for capacity expansion and the merger of wholly owned subsidiary Hyd-Air Engineering into Aeroflex.

segments.name: Metal flexible hoses
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue up 40% YoY, supported by end-user industries and international customers. Current SS hose capacity utilisation is about 80%.

segments.name: Assemblies and other value-added products
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue up 44% YoY, reflecting demand for high-precision engineered flow solutions.

segments.name: Liquid cooling (skid assemblies)
segments.commentary: Contributed 24% of H1 FY27 revenue; management cited skids at upwards of 30% of total revenue. Average realisation per skid was INR3.39 lakhs in Q2. FY27 skid revenue target raised to INR150-200 crores from an initial INR125 crores.

segments.name: Vertical mix
segments.commentary: Data center is now the largest vertical. Ports and terminals is the next growth area, followed by oil and gas and steel. Combined, these verticals are about 26-27% of business, and firefighting plus steel, oil and gas about 30%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 total sales growth of about 60%, with revenue of INR715-725 crores at least.
Skid utilisation expected to reach 40-50% in FY27. Skid capacity is 15,000 units per annum (12,000 commissioned); expansion to 30,000 units per annum by March 2028.
SS hose capacity to rise from 20 million to 30 million meters per annum by March 2028; peak hose-assembly revenue estimated at INR850-900 crores, assuming 70-75% of capacity for assemblies.
Incremental capacity expected to generate INR500-550 crores of revenue per year at peak utilisation; peak utilisation expected in FY30.
FY30 top line guided at about INR1,500 crores versus earlier FY29 target of INR1,000 crores, with EBITDA margins of about 25% and slightly upward.
Hyd-Air merger expected to add at least a couple of percentage points to margins through cost savings; no quantified figure yet. Hyd-Air turnover is about 3% of quarterly Aeroflex turnover.
capex_capacity: Total capex of INR202 crores: INR124 crores for SS flexible flow capacity (brownfield at Taloja plus a proposed new hose-assembly facility) and INR78 crores for skids.
SS flexible flow capacity: 20 million meters per annum completed; further 10 million meters per annum to reach 30 million, due by March 2028.
Skid capacity: 15,000 units per annum expansion due December 2026, with 12,000 units already commissioned; further expansion to 30,000 units by March 2028.
Funding: internal accruals first, then bridge and long-term debt; equity raise only if needed.
Welding automation: two lines added to reduce manual work, raise capacity and reduce rejections. Patent granted for automated 3D CAD model generation of braided hose assemblies.
demand_pricing: Liquid cooling: exclusive arrangement with one large US multinational for the Indian market; no direct bidding to data center end-users. Global liquid cooling market is about $4-5 billion, growing more than 30% YoY; Vertiv is the largest player globally and in India. Indian market size not disclosed.
Visibility: confirmed pipeline of about 3 months (frozen for the current and start of next quarter); longer-term view is an estimate only.

International: advanced-stage sampling and pricing with the same customer, with no timeline given; other international prospects are at an early stage. Realisation expected to be higher than India, not quantified.
Freight and forwarding costs rose significantly on international shipping cost increases. There was no Q1-to-Q2 revenue shift.

qa_highlights.question: Expected cost savings and margin expansion from the Hyd-Air merger?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific number yet; management expects at least a couple of percentage points of margin gain from cost savings, with exact figures after the merger completes.

qa_highlights.question: Is incremental capacity exclusive to the Indian customer?
qa_highlights.answer: Exclusivity for India remains. Capacity is earmarked for customers irrespective of plant, and the remaining capacity is fungible for exports or other customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the skid utilisation outlook for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is expected to reach 40-50% of total skid capacity in FY27, with projections revised monthly or quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY30 and margin targets after the expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Top line of about INR1,500 crores by FY30, with EBITDA margin of about 25% and slightly upward, balancing scale benefits against pricing pressure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and skid outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 sales growth of about 60% (INR715-725 crores at least); skid revenue of INR150-200 crores against the initial INR125 crores target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables grew more slowly than sales, and trade receivable days fell in Q2 and H1 versus last year.

risks_watch: International liquid cooling supply has no timeline; audits, controls and design differences for each country may delay conversion.
Freight and shipping costs have risen sharply and are a major expense driver.
Pricing pressure as the company scales in verticals, which management cites as offsetting scale benefits.
Capex of INR202 crores relies on internal accruals and bridge debt, with equity raise possible if needed.
Skid realisation per unit varies widely (INR1.5 lakhs to INR5 lakhs), so the quarterly average is not a reliable trend.
Management declined to give details on a potential acquisition for products adjacent to SFN, and on the parent company's sanitary valves acquisition.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, capacity and long-term targets, but evasive on quantification: margin uplift from the Hyd-Air merger, international timelines, realisations and India market size were all deferred. Management often gave ranges and said figures would follow later.
key_quotes: We are pleased to report that our best ever results with quarterly revenue crossing INR200 crores milestone for the first time ever.
So, the design actually is completely different.
We expect the realization to be definitely higher than the India market, but it will be too early for me to comment on that.

adds.what: Skid assembly capacity: 15,000 units per annum expansion (12,000 already commissioned)
SS flexible flow capacity: further 10 million meters per annum to reach 30 million (brownfield Taloja plus proposed new hose-assembly facility)
Skid capacity expansion from 15,000 to 30,000 units per annum by March 2028

growth.why: Management guides FY27 sales of INR715-725 crore (~60% growth) and FY30 top line of ~INR1,500 crore, backed by INR202 crore capex (SS hose 20 to 30 million m/yr and skids 15,000 to 30,000 units by March 2028) and a confirmed ~3-month pipeline, though the pipeline visibility beyond that is only an estimate.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 24.27% (H1 23.77% vs 21.19% in H1 FY26), with management guiding FY30 EBITDA margin about 25% and Hyd-Air merger expected to add at least a couple of percentage points, though freight costs are rising and no quantified figure is given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Skid capacity expansion of 15,000 units per annum due December 2026 (12,000 already commissioned), and SS hose capacity 20 to 30 million m/yr due by March 2028, both under construction with INR202 crore total capex.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 sales guided at INR715-725 crore (~60% growth) against H1 FY27 total income of INR353.66 crore (+81%), and skid utilisation expected at 40-50% in FY27 with ~3 months of confirmed pipeline.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 80% overall and SS hose capacity utilisation is about 80%, while the INR202 crore plan already covers capacity to March 2028, so a further phase is plausible but not guided.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance of INR715-725 crore is set as 'at least', and the FY30 target was already raised from INR1,000 crore to INR1,500 crore, but H1 is only INR353.66 crore so the back half must run well above it.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Freight and shipping costs have risen sharply, pricing pressure is expected as verticals scale, and the international liquid cooling timeline is open, so the 60% FY27 growth needs H2 revenue of about INR361-371 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: International liquid cooling sampling and pricing with a large US multinational is advanced but has no timeline, and bellows revenue has only reached INR9 crore in H1 FY27.

rows.label: Liquid cooling skid revenue target raised to INR150-200 crore
rows.why: Skid revenue target raised from INR125 crore to INR150-200 crore, with skids at upwards of 30% of total revenue and 24% of H1 FY27 revenue, supported by an exclusive arrangement with one US multinational for India.

rows.label: International liquid cooling supply
rows.why: Advanced-stage sampling and pricing with the same customer, realisation expected above India, but no timeline and the global liquid cooling market is about $4-5 billion growing above 30%.

rows.label: Hyd-Air Engineering merger into Aeroflex
rows.why: Management expects cost savings adding at least a couple of percentage points to margins, though no figure is quantified and Hyd-Air is only about 3% of quarterly turnover.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 growth of about 60%, skid capacity and the FY30 target of INR1,500 crore, but evasive on quantifying Hyd-Air merger margin gains, international timelines and India market size; analysts pressed on those points and on pricing pressure.
